title: Reflection & plane mirrors
examples: What is the angle of incidence?
How do I draw the reflected ray?
Is the image in a plane mirror real or virtual?

explain.say: Today we are learning about light bouncing off mirrors. This bouncing is called reflection.
The law of reflection is a very important rule to remember. It says the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

draw.text: Angle of incidence = Angle of reflection

explain.say: The angle of incidence is the angle between the incoming ray and the normal. The normal is a line at right angles to the mirror.
A plane mirror always forms a virtual image. This means the image appears to be behind the mirror, but it is not actually there.
If you look into a plane mirror, the image formed is the same size as you. It is also the same distance behind the mirror.
For a real-life example, think about looking at yourself in a calm pond. The water acts like a plane mirror.

draw.text: Pond surface acts like a mirror.

faq.q: What is the normal line when reflecting light?
faq.a: The normal is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the mirror surface at the point where the light hits. It helps us measure the angles correctly.
asks: Where do I draw the normal?
What is the line perpendicular to the mirror?

faq.q: Is the image formed by a plane mirror real or virtual?
faq.a: The image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual. This means light rays only appear to come from that spot, but they do not actually meet there.
asks: Can I catch the image from a mirror?

faq.q: How do I find the angle of reflection?
faq.a: You must first draw the normal line. Then, the angle the reflected ray makes with the normal is the angle of reflection. Remember it matches the angle of incidence.
asks: If the incident angle is 40 degrees, what is the reflection angle?
What is the relationship between the two angles?

faq.q: Does the object size change when I look in a mirror?
faq.a: No, the image formed in a plane mirror has the same size as the object. This is one of the key properties of plane mirrors.
asks: Will the image look bigger or smaller?
Is the image scaled up or down?

faq.q: What is the difference between the incident and reflected ray?
faq.a: The incident ray is the light beam coming towards the mirror. The reflected ray is the light beam bouncing away from the mirror after hitting it.
asks: What is the outgoing ray called?

facts: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
The normal line is always perpendicular to the reflecting surface.
Plane mirrors always form virtual images.
The image formed by a plane mirror is the same size as the object.

quiz.say: If the angle of incidence is 55 degrees, what is the angle of reflection?
quiz.why: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection are always equal.

wrong.0: This is an arbitrary number and does not follow the law of reflection.
wrong.2: This is the angle of the normal, not the reflection angle.
wrong.3: This is a straight line angle, not related to reflection.

quiz.say: What type of image does a plane mirror create?
quiz.why: Plane mirrors reflect light in such a way that the image appears behind the mirror, which is the definition of a virtual image.

wrong.0: Real images are formed where light rays actually meet, which does not happen with plane mirrors.
wrong.1: The image size from a plane mirror is the same as the object, not bigger.
wrong.2: Plane mirrors produce an upright image, not an upside-down one.

quiz.say: If the angle between the incoming ray and the normal is 22 degrees, what is the angle between the reflected ray and the normal?
quiz.why: The angle of reflection must be exactly equal to the angle of incidence, which is 22 degrees.

wrong.1: Angles are measured in degrees, not squared units in this context.
wrong.2: This would only be true if the angle was divided by two, which is incorrect.
wrong.3: This calculation mixes up the angle with the normal line incorrectly.
